reasons: The cited clause 4(a) genuinely reaches the playbook fallback on its material terms: the Customer (AP) may terminate for any reason after the one-year Initial Term on 90 days' notice (inside the 60–90 day fallback window), and the Initial Term is not longer than 12 months, so the 'no Customer convenience right in a multi-year term' walk-away trigger and the 'missing behaviour' deviation are not engaged.

Vendor-side risk is not in walk-away territory: Kubient's convenience right also requires ninety (90) days' notice (not fewer than 90) and cannot be exercised during the Initial Term, so the rule's stated vendor walk-away test is not met.

The 'Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period' language is not a Customer-paid early-termination penalty under the revenue-share model in clause 5; even on the harsher reading (loss of ~90 days of revenue share) it stays within the fallback's 3-months'-fees cap.

Sub-elements short of preferred (90- rather than 30-day Customer notice, no pro-rata prepaid-fee refund mechanic, Vendor right not expressly confined to end of a renewal term) are correctly noted in the rationale rather than flagged, consistent with the classification rules.

The failed deterministic check ('Customer convenience termination present') is a phrasing artefact — the clause uses 'terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term' rather than the words 'for convenience' — and does not undermine the substance.

Consistent with a compliant finding, the redline is identical to the original paragraphs and no counterparty comment is proposed; the rationale also flags the correct trigger to revisit if the term is extended beyond one year.
